title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 244
paragraphs: From no other person was I able to learn anything about this matter; but for the rest I learned as follows by the most diligent inquiry, for I went myself as an eyewitness as far as the city of Elephantine, and from that point onwards I gathered knowledge by report. From Elephantine, as one goes up the river, there is country that slopes steeply; so that here one must attach ropes to the vessel on both sides, as one fastens an ox, and so make one's way onward; and if the rope should break, the vessel is gone at once, swept away by the violence of the stream. Through this country it is a voyage of about four days' length, and in this part the Nile is winding like the river Maeander, and the distance amounts to twelve schoeni, which one must traverse in this manner. Then you come to a level plain, in which the Nile flows around an island named Tachompso. (In the regions above Elephantine, Ethiopians dwell at once successively, who also occupy half of this island, and Egyptians the other half.) Adjoining this island there is a great lake, round which dwell Ethiopian nomad tribes; and when you have sailed through this, you come again to the stream of the Nile, which flows into this lake. After this you disembark and make a journey by land of forty days; for in the Nile sharp rocks stand up out of the water, and there are many reefs, by which it is not possible for a vessel to pass. Then, after you have passed through this country in the forty days I have mentioned, you embark again in another vessel and sail for twelve days; and after this you will come to a great city called Meroë. This city is said to be the mother-city of all the other Ethiopians, and those who dwell in it reverence among the gods Zeus and Dionysus alone, and these they greatly honour; and they have an Oracle of Zeus established, and make warlike marches whenever this god commands them by prophecies, and to whatever place he commands.
